summary: Ghana has admitted all African Union nationals visa-free since January 2025, and ECOWAS citizens move freely under the bloc's protocol; most other visitors still need a visa arranged in advance through a Ghanaian embassy, with a seasonal visa-on-arrival scheme run during the December–January travel season.

fee.notes: Approximate. Fees vary considerably by nationality and by the embassy or high commission handling the application; confirm before applying.
Fee reported at around USD 150 in recent seasons. The scheme is announced year by year, so confirm the current terms with the Ghana Immigration Service before traveling.

passportValidity.text: Your passport should be valid for at least 6 months on the date you arrive in Ghana.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: Proof of yellow fever vaccination is required of all travelers aged 9 months and over and is routinely checked on arrival at Kotoka International Airport.

travelInsurance.text: No insurance requirement is enforced at the border, but medical coverage including evacuation is strongly advised — well-equipped hospitals are limited outside Accra and Kumasi.

onwardTicket.text: Airlines and border officers commonly ask visa-required visitors for a confirmed return or onward ticket; keep proof of accommodation handy as well.

proofOfFunds.text: No fixed amount is published; border officers may ask visitors to show sufficient means for their stay.

currencyLimits.text: Foreign currency worth USD 10,000 or more (or the equivalent) must be declared on arrival and departure.

notes: Drones may not be brought into Ghana without prior authorization from the civil aviation authority — undeclared drones are held at the airport.

payments.text: Cards work at hotels, malls and larger restaurants in Accra and Kumasi, but cash and mobile money dominate everywhere else. Carry cedis for markets, taxis and smaller towns.

safety.text: Ghana is one of West Africa's most stable countries. Petty theft and street scams occur in Accra, and the far-northern border areas adjoining Burkina Faso call for extra caution because of regional insecurity.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Ghana Travel Advisory

bestTimeToVisit.text: November to March is the dry season — hot but with little rain; the Harmattan haze from December to February keeps skies dusty but travel easy, and December is Accra's festive peak season.

idp.text: Ghana is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

tips.text: Since January 2025 Ghana has waived visas for citizens of all African Union countries — African passport holders arrive with just a valid passport and a yellow fever certificate.

Traveling for "Detty December"? Ghana has repeatedly run a seasonal visa-on-arrival scheme for the December–January period. Check gis.gov.gh for the current year's rules before assuming you need an embassy visa.
Carry your yellow fever certificate. It is checked on arrival, and travelers without one risk on-the-spot vaccination at a fee or refusal of entry.
Malaria is present year-round throughout Ghana. Take prophylaxis, use repellent, and stick to bottled or filtered water.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Ghana?
faq.answer: It depends on your passport. Citizens of all African Union countries have entered visa-free since January 2025, and ECOWAS citizens move freely under the bloc's protocol. Most other nationalities — including the US, UK and EU — must obtain a visa in advance from a Ghanaian embassy or high commission.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Ghana?
faq.answer: Yes. US passport holders must obtain a visa before travel from a Ghanaian embassy or consulate — typically a single-entry tourist visa valid for up to 60 days. During the December–January season a visa-on-arrival scheme has been available in recent years.

faq.question: Is Ghana visa-free for African passport holders?
faq.answer: Yes. In January 2025 Ghana abolished visa requirements for citizens of every African Union member state. ECOWAS citizens additionally enjoy free movement with up to 90 days' stay; for other African nationals the permitted stay is set on arrival.

faq.question: Can I get a visa on arrival in Ghana?
faq.answer: Normally no. Visas must be arranged in advance. However, Ghana has run a seasonal visa-on-arrival scheme during the December–January travel season in recent years (around USD 150). The scheme is announced annually, so confirm with the Ghana Immigration Service before relying on it.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever vaccination for Ghana?
faq.answer: Yes. All travelers aged 9 months and over must show a valid yellow fever vaccination certificate on arrival. This applies to every nationality, including visa-free visitors.
